questions.q: cart_total = 99900 (₹999). What does this print?  if cart_total >= 99900: print("free")  else: print("₹49")
questions.explain: >= means 'at least', so exactly 99900 counts. Exactly one of the two blocks runs.

questions.q: Which line is a correct condition to check the coupon code?
questions.explain: == compares; = gives a name to a value (SyntaxError in an if). The line must end with a colon.

questions.q: code = "DIWALI150" and cart_total = 29900 (₹299). Rule: if code == "DIWALI150" and cart_total >= 50000 → ₹150 off. Is it True?
options: False: and needs BOTH parts to be True, and ₹299 is below ₹500
True, because and needs only one part
questions.explain: and = both must be True. or would need only one.

questions.q: In an if / elif / elif / else chain, how many blocks run?
options: Exactly one: the first whose condition is True (or else, if none is)
questions.explain: Python checks from the top and stops at the first True condition. Order matters.

questions.q: A loop does subtotal = price * quantity (with =) for each of Ravi's 3 items. What is subtotal after the loop?
options: Only the LAST item's line total
questions.explain: = replaces the value every round. To add up, use subtotal += price * quantity, with subtotal = 0 before the loop.

questions.q: When should you use while instead of for?
options: When you repeat until something changes (e.g. while stock > 0), not once per item of a collection
When the loop must run exactly 3 times
questions.explain: for walks through a collection (a cart, a list of orders). while repeats as long as a condition stays True.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Which of these values count as False in an if?
questions.explain: Empty or zero-like values are falsy. Non-empty text, even "0" or "False", is truthy.

questions.q: (Going deeper) for wanted in [2, 4, 2, 1, 3] with stock = 5: the loop breaks when stock hits 0. Is the last order (3) ever looked at?
options: No: after selling 2, 2 and 1 (the 4 is refused), stock is 0 and break ends the loop first
questions.explain: break leaves the loop immediately, so later items are never reached. continue would only skip one round.
